text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Friday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Yesterday the parliament adopted at the third reading of the Compulsory Military Service bill. The bill was passed by 66 votes to eight with 11 abstentions.
- The parliament voted to reduce this year's budget deficit to 40 million lats from 59 million.
- About hundred people gathered yesterday near the Monument of Liberators to commemorate the 79th Anniversary of the Great October Revolution.

- On November 12 the Prime Minister will leave for Copenhagen for the meeting of Prime Ministers of the Baltic and Nordic countries. In December he will participate at the summit meeting of EU member states and associated members in Dublin.
- Yesterday in Tallin the Ministers of Interior of the three Baltic Countries discussed the role of the Ministry of Interior in an independent state. The meeting was held behind closed doors.
- In the first nine months of this year the earnings of the Latvian state-owned energy company Latvenergo reached 17.5 million lats.
